workit 13.0.0 — workflow rails for agentic coding

Usage: workit <command> [args] [--json] [--cwd <dir>]

Setup:
  workit init
      Run the interactive setup wizard
  workit setup [--hosts=claude-code,codex,cursor,opencode,pi] [--no-shell] [--dry-run | --yes]
      Write Workit's host permission block after showing the diff; run it in your own terminal
  workit upgrade [--hosts=a,b|none] [--cli] [--preview | --yes | --apply --confirm | --check] [--set-updates=prompt|auto|off] [--json]
      Upgrade the CLI and every host after one confirmation, then verify with doctor; --check compares installed and latest versions
  workit launch <host> [--auto-upgrade] [-- <host args…>]
      Upgrade before host startup, then start the host
  workit doctor [--fix] [--fix-lock [--force [--yes]]]
      Verify the offline installation health (--fix installs the session trailer hook; --fix-lock clears a stale workit store lock)
  workit gc [--dry-run] [--prune-recovery --yes] | --worktrees [--apply] | --branches [--apply] | --procs [--apply]
      Compact long task event logs, drop unreferenced blobs and old check logs; report (or prune) 2.x recovery copies; --worktrees lists (--apply removes) clean worktrees whose work is on the trunk; --branches lists (--apply deletes) local branches whose work is on the trunk; --procs lists (--apply stops) orphaned background processes
  workit dir [plans|retros|handoffs|notes|config|state|data|cache|runtime]
      Print where a kind of file lives (the first four per clone, the rest per user); bare, list the kinds
  workit completion <zsh|bash|fish|powershell>
      Print the shell completion script (setup and upgrade install it for $SHELL); verbs, subcommands, flags, check names, slice ids, workspaces
  workit install --hosts=<h,…> [--preview | --yes]
      Install or repair Workit on the named hosts only
  workit uninstall [--hosts=<h,…> [--preview | --yes]]
      Remove Workit from the picked or named hosts (keeps the Workit config)
  workit grant [show|set|unset] [options]
      Show or change a workspace's autonomy grants (push, pr, merge, release, rerun) and default endpoint; raising needs the user at a terminal
  workit approve <id>…
      Ask the user to approve a Workit request; their yes is recorded once
  workit config show [options]
      Show the effective config here and where each value comes from
  workit workspace [list|add|set|rm|seal] [options]
      Edit workspace entries without the wizard; a raise (rm too) needs the user at a terminal

Task control:
  workit <family> <action> [options]
      Inspect and control a Workit task; <family>: task, policy, evidence, finding, decision, worker, state

Delivery:
  workit check <name> [--full] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--wait <dur> | --no-wait] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] | workit check [--name <n>] [--shell] [--full] [--timeout <s>] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--heavy [--wait <dur> | --no-wait]] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] -- <cmd…> | workit check [--list]
      Run a configured or ad-hoc check and record CLI-observed evidence (exit = the command's); heavy checks wait for the machine-wide heavy-check lease
  workit run --bg [--port <n>] [--name <n>] [--restart <id>] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] -- <cmd…>
      Start a dev server or docker compose up in the background, registered; prints its id, pid, port and log
  workit ps [--all]
      List the registered background processes: id, pid, port, RSS, owner (--all adds ended ones)
  workit stop <id>… | --session <s> | --within <dir> | --orphans [--reason "<why>"]
      Stop registered background processes (the process group: SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 10 s), with a ledger row each
  workit lock status|reap|cancel|wait|run|heavy [options]
      The machine-wide heavy-check lease: who holds it, wait for it, run a command under it, and which shell commands count as heavy
  workit models show [options]
      The model and effort each role (decider, implementer tiers, verifier, reviewer, explore, babysit) runs on for a host, from models.roles, fanout.tierModels and the built-in defaults
  workit pr status|create|template|ready|edit|threads|reply|merge [options]
      PR/MR state with failing log tails and next action; open a SHA-verified PR; mark ready, edit, list and answer review threads; merge only when READY, verified and granted
  workit issue view|comment|close|create [options]
      Read, comment on, close or open a GitHub/GitLab issue on the workspace tracker (or --repo on the same host); writes need the pr grant and are recorded
  workit ci wait|rerun|logs [options]
      Wait for CI on the PR head (exit 0/1/3/4), read the failing jobs' log tails, or rerun failed jobs once per head
  workit git branch|commit|stage|unstage|push|rebase|hold|trailers [options]
      Policy-checked branch, hunk staging and commit (Workit-Session trailer); push with a lease and the tip verified
  workit release start|finish|publish|notes|package [options]

<skill_content name="workit-fanout">
# Skill: workit-fanout

# Fan out parallel workers

Inline-first (workspace `delegation`): fan out only past a threshold, named as
each slice's `reason` (explore, parallel, backstop, high-risk-verify): an
explorer past ~3 tool calls or 10k tokens; parallel writers only for 2+ disjoint
units of ~100+ lines each. Coupled work stays with one owner. Workit never spawns.

1. **Plan the slices** (call the skill tool with `workit-shape`) in a plan file under `workit dir plans`
   (`references/brief.md`): per slice an id, branch, REASON, TIER, SCOPE globs,
   `owns` for shared files, `dependsOn` only for a real dependency, and the brief
   fields. `workit fanout plan <plan.json>` refuses an empty or placeholder brief
   field (exit 2) and two slices that may write one file (exit 3) with a fix; apply it and re-run:
   refuse to spawn while a field is empty or the plan is refused. One PR per
   slice is the default; `"fanIn": "integration"` only when the user wants one
   PR (`references/orchestration.md`).
2. **Record standing orders** (`workit ledger standing add "<order>"`): every
   user directive all workers share. Directives decay across resumes.
3. **Brief each worker verbatim**: `workit fanout worktree create <slice>`
   (every host), then `workit fanout brief <slice>` (WORKTREE, SCRATCH, rules).
   Never hand-edit it; change the plan or the standing orders and render again.
4. **Spawn in a rolling window**, in the background, each in its own worktree:
   keep 4-6 in flight and refill from `spawnable` in `workit fanout status` as
   each one finishes. Assign before spawn (OpenCode: `workit worker assign`); each prompt carries
   the brief, or a pointer: its `WORKER`, `TIER`, `TIMEBOX` and `WORKTREE` lines plus "run `workit fanout brief <slice>` and follow it"
   (budget and model hooks read those lines), so batched OpenCode launches each bind their worker.
   Model: the brief's `model:` and `effort:` lines (`workit models show`), else TIER (`references/orchestration.md`).
   Claude Code: the `implementer` agent; its spawn hook drops `isolation` and refuses a prompt without a WORKTREE line.
5. **Judge liveness by side effects only:** `workit fanout status` (head age,
   PR, CI, verdict, landed; STUCK past the TIMEBOX). Stop a stuck worker and
   observe that it exited (a timeout is not proof); stop a finished one when its
   report arrives (Claude Code: TaskStop). Never two live workers on one branch.
   Removing a worktree drops its uncommitted changes: `workit fanout worktree
   release <slice>` records `git status` in the ledger and refuses without `--force`.
6. **Retry once, then escalate.** A stuck or failed slice gets one retry with
   a fresh brief (`workit fanout brief <slice> --mode resume`, same branch);
   if that fails too, re-slice it, take it over, or report the gap. Never
   chain resumes. A fix round and recheck that both fail: a decider, not a
   third round; product choices go to the user (`references/orchestration.md`).
7. **Verify by the workspace `verification` setting** (`workit grant show`).
   A report is a pointer, never evidence. `proportional` (default): each slice's lane (`workit pr status`) decides; none needs no verdict, self the author's `--self`, focused and full a verifier (Claude Code: the `model` and `effort` of `workit models show --role verifier`) after the last push; one verdict at a stack's top covers its unchanged lower PRs, and a stale one with `reverify: focused` re-checks only the new diff, reusing green CI. `self`: a verifier that wrote none
   of the slices, or you if you wrote none. `independent` or high risk: a
   separate verifier session, never yours (doctrine: the ledger only refuses
   authors). One verifier may take a batch of slices, one verdict per branch
   (`workit ledger verdict <result> --branch <b> --how "<evidence>"`), in a
   session never chosen by the author. Spawn it with the brief's `verifier:` model (`workit models show --role verifier`). A review panel on separate models only at high risk.
8. **Fan in** with `workit fanout check`: out-of-scope files (any file outside
   it stops the fan-in) and `git merge-tree` conflicts with trunk and between
   siblings. Fix what it names until it exits 0; a merged slice reads as
   landed. Then `workit ledger check --branch <b>` per slice, land in `fanout
   status` order, release the worktrees you made, and `workit ledger standing
   clear`. Only you touch topology: workers never rebase, retarget or merge,
   except the integration-tip rebase (integration mode). Then ship
   (call the skill tool with `workit-ship`) up to `defaultEndpoint` from `workit grant show`.

## Example

Bad brief: "Do the API part and add tests." (no scope, acceptance or verify command: nobody can tell when it is done)

Good brief: the output of `workit fanout brief usage-endpoint` (`references/brief.md` shows one).

## Check

```sh
workit fanout check                # exit 0: in scope, no conflicts, landing order printed
workit ledger check --branch <b>   # per slice: accepted (current, passing, independent)
```

<skill_content name="workit-fanout">
# Skill: workit-fanout

# Fan out parallel workers

Inline-first (workspace `delegation`): fan out only past a threshold, named as
each slice's `reason` (explore, parallel, backstop, high-risk-verify): an
explorer past ~3 tool calls or 10k tokens; parallel writers only for 2+ disjoint
units of ~100+ lines each. Coupled work stays with one owner. Workit never spawns.

1. **Plan the slices** (call the skill tool with `workit-shape`) in a plan file under `workit dir plans`
   (`references/brief.md`): per slice an id, branch, REASON, TIER, SCOPE globs,
   `owns` for shared files, `dependsOn` only for a real dependency, and the brief
   fields. `workit fanout plan <plan.json>` refuses an empty or placeholder brief
   field (exit 2) and two slices that may write one file (exit 3) with a fix; apply it and re-run:
   refuse to spawn while a field is empty or the plan is refused. One PR per
   slice is the default; `"fanIn": "integration"` only when the user wants one
   PR (`references/orchestration.md`).
2. **Record standing orders** (`workit ledger standing add "<order>"`): every
   user directive all workers share. Directives decay across resumes.
3. **Brief each worker verbatim**: `workit fanout worktree create <slice>`
   (every host), then `workit fanout brief <slice>` (WORKTREE, SCRATCH, rules).
   Never hand-edit it; change the plan or the standing orders and render again.
4. **Spawn in a rolling window**, in the background, each in its own worktree:
   keep 4-6 in flight and refill from `spawnable` in `workit fanout status` as
   each one finishes. Assign before spawn (OpenCode: `workit worker assign`); each prompt carries
   the brief, or a pointer: its `WORKER`, `TIER`, `TIMEBOX` and `WORKTREE` lines plus "run `workit fanout brief <slice>` and follow it"
   (budget and model hooks read those lines), so batched OpenCode launches each bind their worker.
   Model: the brief's `model:` and `effort:` lines (`workit models show`), else TIER (`references/orchestration.md`).
   Claude Code: the `implementer` agent; its spawn hook drops `isolation` and refuses a prompt without a WORKTREE line.
5. **Judge liveness by side effects only:** `workit fanout status` (head age,
   PR, CI, verdict, landed; STUCK past the TIMEBOX). Stop a stuck worker and
   observe that it exited (a timeout is not proof); stop a finished one when its
   report arrives (Claude Code: TaskStop). Never two live workers on one branch.
   Removing a worktree drops its uncommitted changes: `workit fanout worktree
   release <slice>` records `git status` in the ledger and refuses without `--force`.
6. **Retry once, then escalate.** A stuck or failed slice gets one retry with
   a fresh brief (`workit fanout brief <slice> --mode resume`, same branch);
   if that fails too, re-slice it, take it over, or report the gap. Never
   chain resumes. A fix round and recheck that both fail: a decider, not a
   third round; product choices go to the user (`references/orchestration.md`).
7. **Verify by the workspace `verification` setting** (`workit grant show`).
   A report is a pointer, never evidence. `proportional` (default): each slice's lane (`workit pr status`) decides; none needs no verdict, self the author's `--self`, focused and full a verifier (Claude Code: the `model` and `effort` of `workit models show --role verifier`) after the last push; one verdict at a stack's top covers its unchanged lower PRs, and a stale one with `reverify: focused` re-checks only the new diff, reusing green CI. `self`: a verifier that wrote none
   of the slices, or you if you wrote none. `independent` or high risk: a
   separate verifier session, never yours (doctrine: the ledger only refuses
   authors). One verifier may take a batch of slices, one verdict per branch
   (`workit ledger verdict <result> --branch <b> --how "<evidence>"`), in a
   session never chosen by the author. Spawn it with the brief's `verifier:` model (`workit models show --role verifier`). A review panel on separate models only at high risk.
8. **Fan in** with `workit fanout check`: out-of-scope files (any file outside
   it stops the fan-in) and `git merge-tree` conflicts with trunk and between
   siblings. Fix what it names until it exits 0; a merged slice reads as
   landed. Then `workit ledger check --branch <b>` per slice, land in `fanout
   status` order, release the worktrees you made, and `workit ledger standing
   clear`. Only you touch topology: workers never rebase, retarget or merge,
   except the integration-tip rebase (integration mode). Then ship
   (call the skill tool with `workit-ship`) up to `defaultEndpoint` from `workit grant show`.

## Example

Bad brief: "Do the API part and add tests." (no scope, acceptance or verify command: nobody can tell when it is done)

Good brief: the output of `workit fanout brief usage-endpoint` (`references/brief.md` shows one).

## Check

```sh
workit fanout check                # exit 0: in scope, no conflicts, landing order printed
workit ledger check --branch <b>   # per slice: accepted (current, passing, independent)
```

- Loaded the `workit-fanout` skill and deliberately did **not** create a fan-out plan or register a slice, per your instruction. It also confirmed Workit never spawns workers itself.
- Created the slice worktree and branch:
  - Worktree: `<world>/version-slice`

  - Note: my first attempt used `feat/version-export`; the host branch policy rejected it and required the `feature/` prefix, so I retried with the compliant name.
- Assigned a Workit worker to the slice (`implementer` role, scope `src/version.ts`, stopping condition: file exists with `VERSION = '1.0.0'`, committed on `feature/version-export`, report SHA). Worker assignment id: `bdab5753-f94a-4580-91cf-1796ab99bfcd`.

## Remaining

- After the worker reports: verify the file content and commit exist on `feature/version-export` (read/git log, not by writing the file myself), then report the result. Worker reports are pointers, not evidence.
- Optionally release the worktree (`git worktree remove …` / cleanup) once the slice is accepted.

Spawn one subagent with a prompt like:

```
WORKER: bdab5753-f94a-4580-91cf-1796ab99bfcd

WORKTREE: <world>/version-slice
BRANCH: feature/version-export

Work only in WORKTREE. Create src/version.ts containing exactly:
export const VERSION = '1.0.0';
Commit it on feature/version-export with a clear message. Do not touch other files. Report the commit SHA.
```
